bootstrap: arbitration._boot: 10,000 resamples, seed 0, percentile, paired over items

task1_exceedance.definition: An item is EXCEEDABLE only if neither deterministic source already ranks the gold first. If either does, that source scores RR=1.0 and top-1=1.0, the ceiling, so 'beats the better of its two sources' is arithmetically impossible there and the item carries no information about integration.

control_cell_limitation.reading: The control cell is defined by margin<=0, i.e. annotation is non-discriminating BY CONSTRUCTION: 19/20 items have all six annotation scores tied (ann_rank 3.5), the 20th has the gold below a tie group. There is therefore no second signal to integrate. The cell tests NON-DISTRACTION (does the model abandon a good source when a useless one is named reliable?) -- it cannot test integration, and its 100 item-arm cells should not enter an integration denominator. A further artifact: scoring the annotation-only ranker as 1/avg_rank gives MRR 0.281, BELOW chance 0.408, when a random tie-break scores exactly chance. The reported '+0.42 over annotation-only' in control is ~0.29 once ties are handled as ties.

conflict.note: noise_floor.json's 0.911 is GOLD-RANK agreement (it compares reciprocal ranks), not full-ordering agreement. The paper must not cite it as the latter.

uniform_720_STRAWMAN.description: P(match a specified 6-permutation) = 1/720 per call, i.i.d.
uniform_720_STRAWMAN.verdict: STRAWMAN -- do not use. No LLM samples uniformly over orderings; it samples from a sharply peaked distribution concentrated on evidence-consistent orders. Rejecting uniformity is uninformative and a reviewer will say so.

entropy_only.description: Could low sampling entropy alone explain 39/40? Self-agreement bounds how concentrated the output distribution is, but says NOTHING about WHICH ordering it concentrates on. A model that deterministically emitted any other fixed ordering would show the same self-agreement and 0/40 external matches. Entropy and mode identity are logically independent.
entropy_only.headline: At forced T=1 model B reproduces ITS OWN full six-item ordering on only 0.575 of re-sampled conflict calls, yet reproduces an EXTERNAL deterministic ranker's full ordering on 39/40 = 0.975 of control calls. It agrees with the phenotype ranker more than it agrees with itself.
entropy_only.caveat: Two caveats a reviewer will raise, and they are fair. (1) Model B's retest covers the CONFLICT cell only (80 calls); control-cell self-agreement was never measured, so we cannot exclude that control calls are simply near-zero-entropy. (2) The two cells differ in difficulty, so 0.575 vs 0.975 is not a matched comparison. Neither caveat rescues an entropy explanation: low entropy still leaves open WHICH ordering is the mode, and the finding is that the mode is the external ranker's output.
entropy_only.verdict: Not a competing explanation; it constrains stability, not target.

matched_entropy_bound.description: Suppose the control calls had the SAME output entropy as the measured conflict calls. Full-ordering self-agreement 0.575 is the collision probability sum(p_i^2); concentrating as much mass as possible on a single ordering gives p_mode <= sqrt(0.575).
matched_entropy_bound.verdict: Even the most deterministic reading of the measured entropy caps the match rate at ~0.76, below the observed 0.975. Conditional on the conflict-cell entropy transferring -- which is unverified, since no control retest exists.

within_model_cell_contrast.description: The defensible null. Same model, same deployment, same forced T=1, same tool stack, same prompt -- only the EVIDENCE differs. If the 39/40 control match were a decoding/entropy artifact it would hold in the conflict cell too. It does not.
within_model_cell_contrast.verdict: Use this one. It is a real empirical contrast, not a coin-flip null.

confound_checks.note: If the phenotype-only ordering coincided with the order the candidates were listed in, matching it would be trivial. It does not, so the match is to the numeric evidence.
